readback.name: Poincare.DeTurckDifferentialSymmetry.differential_and_lower_symmetric
readback.mathematical_statement:
For every universe u, let M be an arbitrary topological Hausdorff manifold with charts modeled on E = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) and a C∞ manifold structure for the boundaryless model 𝓡 3. Bilin is E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ, Jet1 is E →L[ℝ] Bilin, Jet2 is E →L[ℝ] Jet1, and Variables is (Bilin × Jet1) × Jet2. The leading letI binders fix the usual real operator-norm additive-group and real normed-space structures on Jet1, E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] E, E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] E, and Jet2. They fix the usual product normed-group and real normed-space structures on Bilin × Jet1 and Variables, and the usual product additive commutative monoid on Bilin × Jet1. These are specified canonical structures, rather than arbitrary norm choices.

Let g0 and bg be actual C∞ Riemannian metrics on M, with symmetric continuous bilinear tangent-fiber forms, positivity on every nonzero tangent vector, bounded unit balls in the Riemannian sense, and smooth dependence as bundle sections. Fix arbitrary anchor : M, total coefficient map q : E → Bilin, and point z : E. Assume z belongs to the anchor extended-chart target, the chosen GeodesicTransport.cutoff(anchor) equals 1 eventually in a neighborhood of z, q is C² at z, and eventually near z one has q(y)(v,w) = q(y)(w,v) for every v,w : E. The neighborhood symmetry hypothesis has the quantifiers eventually y, then for all tensor vectors v,w. There is no positivity, compact-support, or global-smoothness premise for q, and no separate supplied Hessian or covariance certificate.

Set G0(y) to the actual chart metric of g0, obtained by applying its tangent-fiber metric to the two inverse-chart tangent derivatives. Set B(y) to the background chart Christoffel field of bg, defined using the globally blended chart metric cutoff(y)·chartMetric(bg)(y) + (1-cutoff(y))·EuclideanMetric. B and DB = fderiv ℝ B are fixed background data in the metric linearization. At z write G = G0(z), J0 = DG0(z), H0 = D²G0(z), h = q(z), Jq = Dq(z), and Hq = D²q(z), with D² meaning the ordered fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ·). Let e_i be the standard Euclidean basis, A_ij the inverse of the matrix G(e_i,e_j), and δA_ij(h) = -Σ_k Σ_l A_ik·h(e_k,e_l)·A_lj. Define K = fderiv ℝ ((G',J') ↦ lowerTerm(B(z),DB(z),G',J')) at (G,J0). The full output is exactly Σ_i Σ_j δA_ij(h)·H0(e_i,e_j) + Σ_i Σ_j A_ij·Hq(e_i,e_j) + K(h,Jq). Thus the inverse-variation term against the base second jet H0 is retained, and the principal second-q-derivative contraction has a positive sign.

The declared zeroOrder map on h is Σ_i Σ_j δA_ij(h)·H0(e_i,e_j) + K(h,0). The firstOrder map on Jq is K(0,Jq). The declared lower output is their sum, equivalently Σ_i Σ_j δA_ij(h)·H0(e_i,e_j) + K(h,Jq). It omits the principal contraction of Hq, but still contains the inverse variation against H0. Neither zeroOrder nor firstOrder is a newly assumed coefficient or a map certified symmetric by an input premise.

For completeness, lowerTerm(B,DB,G',J')(v,w) = -2·R(G',J')(v,w) + J'(W)(v,w) + G'(U(v),w) + G'(v,U(w)). Its ingredients are the pinned finite-jet definitions. Write κ_J(x,y)(s) = ½[J'(x)(y,s)+J'(y)(x,s)-J'(s)(x,y)] and Γ(u,v) = (G')⁻¹(κ_J(v,u)), preserving that argument order. For b = Module.finBasis ℝ E and r_i = (G')⁻¹(b.coord_i), W = Σ_i [Γ(r_i,b_i)-B(r_i,b_i)]. Set dr_i(a) = -(G')⁻¹(J'(a)(r_i,·)). Then U(a) = Σ_i [-(G')⁻¹(J'(a)(Γ(r_i,b_i),·)) + Γ(dr_i(a),b_i) - DB(a)(r_i,b_i) - B(dr_i(a),b_i)]. Finally R(v,w) = Σ_i b.coord_i [-(G')⁻¹(J'(b_i)(Γ(v,w),·)) + (G')⁻¹(J'(v)(Γ(b_i,w),·)) + Γ(b_i,Γ(v,w)) - Γ(v,Γ(b_i,w))]. Here (G')⁻¹ in those formulas is the continuous bilinear-form inverse operator used by the definitions. Consequently the full operator is the finite-jet linearization associated with the spatial DeTurck sign -2 Ricci + Lie; the statement has no time derivative or negative principal operator.

The conclusion is the conjunction of two tensor-slot symmetry claims: for every v,w : E, full(v,w) = full(w,v), and independently for every v,w : E, lower(v,w) = lower(w,v). Each quantifier ranges over all model-space vectors, not just basis vectors. It concerns the outputs on the actual value and derivatives of a locally symmetric C² q at the actual smooth-metric base. It does not state that these coefficient maps preserve symmetry for unrestricted arbitrary jet inputs, does not assert any interchange of spatial derivative directions as its conclusion, and does not separately prove a HasFDerivAt certificate for K or the nonlinear evolution. There is no premise assuming either requested output symmetry, so the result is not a circular symmetry wrapper. No second chart, partition, time horizon, Hölder norm, compactness of M, connectedness, flow existence, or Poincare conclusion is part of this statement.
